q: Officer reasons backward: victims freed, contractor acquitted for lack of trafficking proof. What missing link must SI have secured at rescue?
options: Age proof, statements, transport and payment trail to prove coercion and movement
expl: Reverse-engineer needs proof chain. Movement plus exploitation proves trafficking.
why: Acquittal often comes from weak rescue documentation. SI must lock corridor evidence early.
trapnote: Rescue without paper fails in court.

q: Claim: fee for pilgrim bus and tax to promote one faith are both barred as religious levy. Flaw?
options: Half-truth, fee for service used is allowed, tax for faith is barred
expl: Half-truth merges fee with tax. Service return saves fee.
why: Analytical eye checks quid pro quo. Bus charge pays for ride, not belief.

q: Aided school compels prayer vs pupil cites culture and admission guard. Headmaster cites management right. How to resolve collision?
options: Aided needs consent for compulsion, cannot deny on identity, management subject to both
expl: Cross-article collision balances autonomy with conscience and admission guard.
why: No right is absolute. Consent and non-denial fence management discretion.

q: Trafficked child rescued, denied schooling, family threatened, officer inactive. What chain reaction follows if SI delays?
options: Exploitation continues, welfare lost, detention claim plus duty order against inaction
expl: Delay triggers criminal, welfare and remedy consequences together.
why: Chain thinking shows inaction breeds multiple liabilities. Prompt rescue breaks cycle.

q: Statement set looks all correct on tax, schools, minorities and writs but one line says State assembly can punish for these rights. Verdict?
options: Fails on exclusivity, only Parliament can legislate there
why: Analytical check hunts sole outlier. Exclusivity is easy to miss in long set.

q: New criminal codes replace old laws on trafficking and add safeguards for night arrest of women and remand. What does SI update in rescue SOP?
options: Register under new trafficking law, follow night-arrest safeguard, produce timely for remand
Arrest women at night without safeguard
expl: BNS-BNSS 2023-24 update trafficking, night safeguard and remand.
why: Current SOP must cite new law. Safeguards and timelines protect both victim and case.

q: AP now has 26 districts after 2022 reorganisation. Trafficking bus crosses three new districts. Implication for SI?
options: Coordinate FIR across districts and alert new SPs, jurisdiction follows route
expl: 26 districts need cross-district coordination and zero-FIR transfer.
why: Reorganisation changes maps not duty. Route coordination secures victims and evidence.

q: In Nov 2022 a Constitution Bench upheld EWS quota. Minority college claims EWS law forces its admissions. Correct link to minority shield?
options: EWS upheld generally but quota law under special clause skips minority institutions
expl: Janhit Abhiyan Nov 2022 upheld EWS, special quota clause excludes minorities.
why: Current plus old law combine. General validity does not erase minority exclusion.

q: A 2024 nine-judge ruling read private resources into a Directive word broadly. Debater says it ends minority school autonomy. Correct caution?
options: No, broad reading does not erase establish-administer shield, apply case specifically
expl: 2024 39(b) ruling is specific, minority autonomy remains.
why: Current rulings need narrow reading. Do not stretch resource logic to kill school rights.

q: 106th Amendment 2023 gives one-third seats to women, operative after census and delimitation. Protester says it already reserves temple trusts. Reply?
options: Operative only after census-delimitation for legislatures, not temple trusts
Operative at once for all bodies
expl: 106th Amendment 2023 waits on census and delimitation, legislature only.
why: Timing and scope both limited. Do not extend seat quota to religious management.
